headline_conclusions: The embedding model is the dominant factor in post-processing quality: Contriever-msmarco enables effective similarity filtering, while all-MiniLM-L6-v2 collapses under the fixed tau = 0.6 threshold.
Under Contriever embeddings, dot product outperforms cosine similarity on TriviaQA (0.7941 vs 0.7187 with semantic chunking), especially when chunk length is heterogeneous.
Semantic and fixed-size chunking perform comparably on these short-context benchmarks; semantic chunking is expected to help more on longer, structurally complex documents.

findings.title: MiniLM post-processing collapses under a fixed threshold
findings.summary: Adding similarity filtering with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sharply lowers BERTScore. Semantic + MiniLM falls from 0.8019 (No PP) to 0.6083 on TriviaQA; fixed-size falls from 0.8022 to 0.5563. The same collapse appears on SQuAD (0.8366 to 0.6154).
findings.explanation: MiniLM is a lightweight sentence-pair model and tends to assign systematically lower similarity to valid answer-chunk pairs. With a fixed tau = 0.6, many correctly grounded answers fall below threshold and are discarded as 'no context provided', driving up false negatives and lowering both precision and recall.

findings.title: Contriever is the right encoder for the validation step
findings.summary: With Contriever-msmarco, filtering stays competitive: semantic cosine 0.7187 and dot 0.7941 on TriviaQA; fixed-size 0.6815 and 0.7925. Dot product nearly matches the No-PP baseline while still filtering hallucinations.
findings.explanation: Contriever was trained with a contrastive objective on passage retrieval, so its embedding space is better calibrated for measuring answer-to-passage alignment. The threshold tau is therefore not universal — it must be calibrated to the score distribution of the chosen embedding model.

findings.title: Cosine = dot for MiniLM; dot wins for Contriever
findings.summary: MiniLM yields identical scores for cosine and dot product across every configuration. Contriever shows a real gap, largest on TriviaQA fixed-size: cosine 0.6815 vs dot 0.7925 (delta 0.0754).
findings.explanation: MiniLM L2-normalises embeddings by default, so for unit vectors cosine and dot product are algebraically the same and produce identical rankings. Contriever embeddings are not perfectly normalised; longer, denser chunks get larger magnitudes, and dot product's magnitude sensitivity rewards those relevant chunks, more so under heterogeneous fixed-size chunks.

findings.title: Chunking strategy barely moves the needle here
findings.summary: Without post-processing, fixed-size is marginally higher on both datasets. With Contriever dot-product, semantic leads on TriviaQA (0.7941 vs 0.7925) while fixed-size edges SQuAD (0.8378 vs 0.8365). Differences are small.
findings.explanation: TriviaQA and SQuAD are short-context benchmarks, so 512-token fixed chunks usually already contain the evidence without splitting it. On long, structured scientific documents, semantic chunking's topical coherence is expected to matter much more. Fixed-size also produces many more chunks, increasing generation time on a single GPU.

findings.title: SQuAD scores higher than TriviaQA everywhere
findings.summary: Across all 12 configurations SQuAD beats TriviaQA. Example: Contriever dot semantic is 0.7941 (TriviaQA) vs 0.8365 (SQuAD).
findings.explanation: SQuAD is extractive — the gold answer is a span present verbatim in the provided passage, so Zephyr-7B-Beta matches reference phrasing closely. TriviaQA needs cross-sentence reasoning over longer, web-sourced contexts, making generation and reference matching harder. The MiniLM collapse still hits SQuAD, confirming threshold miscalibration (not dataset difficulty) is the main driver.

behavioural_notes.caveat: A higher raw BERTScore for No-PP does not necessarily mean better grounding — without filtering, the model may return fluent answers from parametric memory rather than genuinely grounded ones. That is exactly the hallucination risk the similarity filter is meant to catch.
behavioural_notes.abstention: TriviaQA abstention ('no context provided') ranges from 13.2% (Contriever + Fixed + Dot) to 35.8% (MiniLM + Fixed). Fewer answers attempted is not automatically safer.

limitations: Preliminary sample sizes are small (5-50 per configuration), introducing variance.
Standard RAG baselines (RAG + MiniLM, RAG + Contriever, RAG + Reranker) are not yet implemented.
Fixed tau = 0.6 is not calibrated per embedding model; MiniLM likely needs a lower threshold.
Per-question latency was not yet recorded systematically for a cost comparison.
next_steps: Scale to at least 200 samples per configuration per dataset.
Implement the full set of standard RAG baselines with the same Zephyr-7B-Beta generator.
Examine MiniLM vs Contriever similarity-score distributions to derive a model-specific threshold.
Record processing time per configuration for a fair computational-cost comparison.
